subject: chemistry
question_text: Which of the two ions Ca²⁺ or Zn²⁺ is more stable? Why?

verification.note: Chapter 3 is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.56-61), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. NOTATION: the book prints the ion charges as Ca⁺² and Zn⁺²; the card uses the standard Ca²⁺ and Zn²⁺.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The two configurations
steps.why: The whole comparison rests on the two electron arrangements, so they are written first. One is a true noble gas arrangement; the other only resembles one.
common_mistakes: Writing Zn²⁺ as 2, 8, 8, 2 — the ion has lost the two 4s electrons, leaving 2, 8, 18.
Calling the 18-electron arrangement an inert gas configuration. It is a pseudo inert gas configuration.
steps.memory_tip: Ca²⁺ matches argon exactly. Zn²⁺ ends in 18, which matches no noble gas.
steps.margin_note: Write both configurations in shell form. The numbers are the argument.

steps.label: The answer with reason

lines.text: Ca²⁺ is more stable than Zn²⁺

lines: Ca²⁺ has a true inert gas configuration,
which is more stable than the pseudo
steps.why: A true inert gas configuration is the most stable electron arrangement. The 18 outer electrons of a pseudo inert gas configuration shield the nucleus poorly, so that arrangement is less stable.
common_mistakes: Answering Zn²⁺ because 18 is a larger number than 8. More outer electrons does not mean more stable.
steps.memory_tip: A true noble gas arrangement is more stable than a pseudo one.
steps.margin_note: Name both configurations in the reason. The comparison is the mark.

insider_note: The mark is in the word pseudo — saying Zn²⁺ has 18 outer electrons without naming the pseudo inert gas configuration loses the reason mark.
